scope: All claims in the existing public Anduril case with public supporting locators. This is one worked example, not the whole corpus or a new independent review.
boundary: The categorical orientation is an editorial reporting aperture, not a score. Lobbying, PAC activity, former-official experience, acquisitions, shared personnel, temporal sequence, and product integration do not establish influence, causation, coordination, control, wrongdoing, or unlawful procurement. A causal claim requires decision-specific communications or signed records.
disclaimer: No wrongdoing is alleged. A ceiling is not an obligation; a prototype is not acceptance; installed capacity is not qualified output; an open interface is not government-owned substitution authority; and a source's silence is not proof of absence.

records.plain: Anduril's 2025 second-quarter lobbying filing reported $700,000 in expense and named work on the Autonomous Surveillance Towers program, H.R. 1, appropriations, acquisition policy, rocket motors, connected warfare and command and control, strike, space, maritime, export controls, and foreign military sales.
records.qualification: The filing proves disclosed lobbying activity, not authorship of legislation, influence on a decision, or award causation.

receipts.label: Anduril Industries 2025 Q2 LD-2
receipts.notes: Establishes disclosed lobbying expense, lobbyists, issues, and contacted institutions; not authorship, influence, or award causation.

records.plain: The FEC identifies an active Anduril corporate PAC; for the reporting period cited in the bundle it showed $202,217.33 in receipts, $172,233.95 in disbursements, and $166,000 in contributions to other committees, with no independent expenditures.
records.qualification: Recipient-level Schedule B records are required before drawing candidate- or committee-specific conclusions. Contributions do not prove quid pro quo.

receipts.label: Anduril Industries, Inc. Political Action Committee overview
receipts.notes: Establishes committee status and aggregate reporting. Recipient-level records are required for candidate-specific analysis.

records.plain: Anduril's biography for Gregory Kausner describes prior senior acquisition, security-cooperation, State Department, Senate, DIU, and Navy roles before he joined the company to lead global defense work.
records.qualification: Government experience identifies expertise and access-relevant knowledge. It does not prove preferential treatment.

receipts.label: Anduril welcomes Gregory Kausner as Head of Global Defense
receipts.notes: Company biography; dates and duties should be checked against official records before publication.

records.plain: The Army identifies Michael Obadal as Under Secretary of the Army with responsibilities that include acquisition strategy and enterprise reform after his prior Anduril employment.
records.qualification: The official biography does not establish participation in a particular Anduril matter, an ethics violation, or the content of any recusal or waiver.

receipts.label: Under Secretary of the Army biography: Michael Obadal
receipts.notes: Confirms appointment and public responsibilities; does not supply the ethics file or establish participation in any particular matter.

records.plain: Anduril announced that its acquisition of Area-I added the ALTIUS family of air-launched effects to its hardware portfolio.
records.qualification: The company statement establishes its transaction account, not the transaction terms, inherited SBIR rights, government acceptance, or later operational performance.

receipts.label: Anduril acquires Area-I and adds ALTIUS capabilities
receipts.notes: Company description of the transaction and intended portfolio effect; transaction terms and government lineage require separate records.

records.plain: Anduril announced that its acquisition of Adranos created its solid-rocket-motor business.
records.qualification: The company statement does not establish qualification, yield, accepted output, customer demand, or delivery performance.

receipts.label: Anduril acquires solid rocket motor manufacturer Adranos
receipts.notes: Company description; transaction terms and qualification, yield, and delivery performance are not established.

records.plain: Anduril announced that acquiring Numerica's radar and command-and-control businesses brought radar, tracking algorithms, and C2 capabilities in-house for integration into Lattice.
records.qualification: The announcement does not establish completed integration, government acceptance, or a causal link to NGC2.

receipts.label: Anduril acquires Numerica radar and command-and-control businesses
receipts.notes: Company statement that the capabilities would be integrated into Lattice; it does not establish completed integration or government acceptance.

records.plain: DoD announced a $14.3 million Defense Production Act Title III award for solid-rocket-motor capacity, building on a stated $75 million Anduril private investment.
records.qualification: Capacity support is not qualification, yield, accepted output, delivery, or a guaranteed production award.

receipts.label: DoD awards $14.3 million to expand solid rocket motor sources
receipts.notes: Establishes the DPA award and stated private investment; capacity investment is not qualification, accepted output, yield, or delivery.

records.plain: The March 2026 Army enterprise contract is a single-award, ten-year IDIQ with a $20 billion ceiling for Anduril's full commercial suite.
records.qualification: The $20 billion figure is a maximum ceiling, not committed revenue or obligated funds.

receipts.label: SAM.gov award and justification notice W9128Z-26-D-A001
receipts.notes: Establishes the vehicle and ceiling; the $20 billion ceiling is not an obligation.

receipts.label: U.S. Army awards enterprise contract for IT commercial solutions
receipts.notes: Establishes the Army's description of the consolidation; does not contain the complete J&A, price schedule, ordering guide, or data-rights terms.

records.plain: The Army said the enterprise contract consolidated more than 120 Anduril procurement actions into one framework.
records.qualification: The announcement does not disclose the complete source-selection, pricing, ordering, new-item, data-rights, or substitution rules.

receipts.label: U.S. Army awards enterprise contract for IT commercial solutions
receipts.notes: Establishes the Army's description of the consolidation; does not contain the complete J&A, price schedule, ordering guide, or data-rights terms.

records.plain: The Army announced that Anduril leads the NGC2 common-data baseline, with Palantir retained for the Lattice-Foundry data mesh and Raft supplying registries, transformation, and federation.
records.qualification: The announcement does not establish government ownership of all schemas, interfaces, deployment tools, data rights, or a completed removal-and-substitution test.

receipts.label: Army establishes NGC2 common data baseline
receipts.notes: Establishes the announced roles; does not disclose the complete contractual instrument, acceptance criteria, data rights, or removal test.

records.plain: Public Law 119-21 restricted specified border-technology funds to surveillance towers already tested and accepted by CBP to deliver autonomous capabilities.
records.qualification: The law does not name Anduril or establish who proposed, drafted, or intended the language.

receipts.label: Public Law 119-21, section 90004
receipts.notes: Establishes the tested-and-accepted eligibility condition; does not identify the author or beneficiary.

records.plain: CBP placed a $362,974,500 tower order on 25 December 2025 under parent IDIQ 70B02C20D00000019.
records.qualification: The award record does not establish who authored the statutory gate, whether CBP considered no alternatives, or whether lobbying caused the order.

receipts.label: USAspending order 70B02C26F00000035
receipts.notes: Establishes the disclosed amount and parent vehicle; not the alternatives analysis or exact appropriation trace.

records.plain: USAspending describes FA882024DB001 as an SBIR III follow-on single-award IDIQ for Lattice mesh networking.
records.qualification: The public record does not by itself establish government substitutability, all child-order scope, or that the entire ceiling will be used.

receipts.label: USAspending IDIQ FA882024DB001
receipts.notes: Establishes the disclosed vehicle description and child-award snapshot; full lineage, pricing, data rights, and sustainment records remain necessary.

records.plain: Anduril describes the Space Surveillance Network path as moving from earlier innovation work into a Program of Record.
records.qualification: The government award, lineage, test, acceptance, price, and data-rights files control.

receipts.label: Anduril awarded Program of Record Space Surveillance Network
receipts.notes: Company description of the transition path; government award files control.

records.plain: The Marine Corps installation counter-UAS IDIQ had a $642.21 million maximum and was competitively procured with ten offers.
records.qualification: This is a counterexample to a claim that every large Anduril award followed a sole-source path. The ceiling is not an obligation.

receipts.label: DoD Contracts for March 7, 2025
receipts.notes: Establishes a competitive ten-offer award and ceiling; the ceiling is not an obligation.

records.plain: NCIA awarded first-phase eAirC2 work to Anduril, Palantir, and Athea for evaluation before a long-term selection.
records.qualification: Amounts, detailed criteria, scoring, and the final selection are not disclosed in this announcement.

receipts.label: NCIA awards first-phase eAirC2 contracts
receipts.notes: Establishes the three-vendor evaluation; detailed criteria, values, and final scoring are not disclosed.

records.plain: GAO denied Anduril's 2021 protest challenging the scope and competitive category of an Air Force tactical-edge solicitation.
records.qualification: A denied protest does not establish abuse of protest rights or a general rule about the company's access.

receipts.label: GAO B-419420, Anduril Industries
receipts.notes: Program-specific protest decision; does not establish a general rule about the company.

records.plain: GAO's Digital Force decision records that the Air Force initially issued simultaneous Phase III solicitations to Clear Align and Anduril, canceled both as corrective action, and later proceeded with Clear Align.
records.qualification: The decision is program-specific and demonstrates that inclusion in an initial Phase III path did not guarantee Anduril the final solicitation.

receipts.label: GAO B-423319, Digital Force Technologies
receipts.notes: Program-specific corrective-action and lineage record; Anduril was not the protester in the final decision.

records.plain: Australian Defence stated in April 2026 that Navy had taken delivery of Ghost Shark autonomous underwater vehicles.
records.qualification: The release does not disclose delivery count, acceptance conditions, deficiencies, mission readiness, or availability.

receipts.label: Australian Defence prepares for new National Defence Strategy
receipts.notes: Establishes the government's delivery statement; not delivery count, acceptance conditions, deficiencies, or operational availability.

records.plain: Anduril describes Ghost Shark as a co-funded prototype-to-Program-of-Record path, making it a useful comparison with less visible sole-source or enterprise transitions.
records.qualification: The comparison does not establish operational success or the absence of dependence, deficiencies, or rights disputes.

receipts.label: Ghost Shark enters Program of Record
receipts.notes: Company account of the co-development-to-fleet path; contract, milestone, and acceptance records control.

receipts.label: Australian Defence prepares for new National Defence Strategy
receipts.notes: Establishes the government's delivery statement; not delivery count, acceptance conditions, deficiencies, or operational availability.
